titleStmt.title: Proposed regulations concerning the taking animals by fishing, by hunting, or otherwise, on the shores of and off the coasts of all the islands of Hokkaido and of those adjacent thereto wider the jurisdiction of the empire of Japan.

head.hi: Proposed regulations concerning the taking animals by fishing, by hunting, or otherwise, on the shores of and off the coasts of all the islands of Hokkaido and of those adjacent thereto wider the jurisdiction of the empire of Japan.

list.label: I.
list.item: Every foreign vessel is prohibited from taking fish or other marine animals, either by the use of hooks and lines, or of nets, by shooting them, or in any other way whatever, within reach of a cannon-shot from the shore of any of the coasts of all the islands of Hokkaido and of those adjacent thereto belonging to this empire.
list.label: II.
list.item: It shall be the duty of the Japanese officers specially appointed for the purpose to warn the vessel to leave the place when they have cause to believe her to be violating or to be preparing to violate this prohibition; and if a foreign vessel be found to have violated this prohibition, the said officers shall have the right to board such foreign vessel and to examine her cargo.
list.label: III.
list.item: Whenever any foreign vessel has violated the prohibition contained in the first article, and whenever she shall refuse to leave the place or to allow the examination of her cargo, as mentioned in the second article, it shall be lawful for the officers mentioned in the above article to bring such vessel into the nearest open port, where she shall be placed in charge of the consul of her nationality, and, upon examination, if she be proved guilty, she shall be condemned to make proper reparation.
